keyword: how do astronauts go to the bathroom
claims: Astronauts use the Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) on the International Space Station.
The Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) relies on air suction rather than gravity to collect waste.
The Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) uses a funnel for urine.
The Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) uses a small seat with suction for solid waste.
Foot restraints and handholds are used to keep astronauts positioned in microgravity.
Airflow draws waste into containers to prevent it from floating away.
Solid waste is stored in bags that are sealed.
Solid waste is eventually disposed of upon reentry.
On the International Space Station, urine is processed through the Urine Processing Assembly (UPA) to be turned back into potable water.
The toilet is located in a private, enclosed compartment.
The Artemis II flight is a 10-day flight.
For shorter missions such as the Artemis II flight, urine is vented into space instead of being recycled
